name: Ukraine

facts.religion: Orthodox Christian about 70%, Greek Catholic about 9%

system_note: Under martial law since 2022, which suspends elections.
snapshot: A brief US-brokered ceasefire in May collapsed within days, and the war ground on along a 745-mile front as both sides escalated long-range strikes.
culture: Ukrainian identity has strengthened sharply since 2014, and especially since 2022, with many people switching from Russian to Ukrainian. Embroidered vyshyvanka shirts, borscht, which is UNESCO-listed, and Cossack history are symbols of pride. Ukraine won Eurovision in 2016 and 2022. Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral dates to the 11th century.
society: Russia's full-scale invasion has killed tens of thousands of civilians and soldiers, displaced millions and occupied about a fifth of the country. Ukraine has become a world leader in drone warfare. The economy depends on Western aid. Corruption scandals, including one in the energy sector in 2025, remain sensitive.
situation: Russia's full-scale invasion has now lasted more than four and a half years, longer than the Soviet Union's war against Nazi Germany. Russia holds about a fifth of Ukraine. In 2026 the war did not end, but the effort to end it kept being interrupted by other crises.

A US-brokered ceasefire for 9 to 11 May was broken almost at once, with each side accusing the other of thousands of violations and fighting continuing along a 745-mile front (Reuters via Defense News). Washington's peace push stalled in March when its attention shifted to the war with Iran. Russia's foreign minister declared in August that "there will be no ceasefire," and Moscow kept demanding Ukraine hand over parts of the east its troops have not captured. Meanwhile, both sides escalated long-range strikes: the UN counted 15,280 civilian casualties in the first eight months of 2026, up 55 percent on the year before, the worst since the early days of the war (Political.org tracker). In September, the Kremlin said three-way talks with Ukraine and the US could resume in October, and Zelensky said he would meet Putin at the G20 summit in Miami in December (AFP via Ahram). Forecasters put the chance of a ceasefire this year at about 15 percent. For Ukrainians, the reality is another winter of attacks on power plants and homes.
power: A semi-presidential republic under martial law since 2022, which has suspended elections. The president leads foreign and defence policy; the prime minister and cabinet answer to the 450-seat Verkhovna Rada.
holders: President Volodymyr Zelensky, in office since 2019, with Kyrylo Budanov as head of the presidential office.

update.html: On 21 October Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff he agreed in principle to resume three-way talks with Ukraine on or after 10 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi, and Zelensky backed the format. On 23 October the two sides agreed a local humanitarian ceasefire in occupied Oleshky, mediated by Melania Trump, and swapped 270 prisoners each. Hungary lifted its block on Ukraine's EU accession talks on 16 October. On the ground, Ukraine has regained a little territory since September, though Russian troops are about 9 km from Kramatorsk.
